minutes.headline: Committee ratified a one-year, 4% para-professional contract and set FY26 capital-plan priority rankings.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee heard a proposal for a new education foundation (LEAF), reviewed back-to-school hiring and enrollment updates, and discussed FY26 budget timeline concerns including staff retention and salary competitiveness. The committee ratified a one-year para-professional contract, approved FY26 capital-plan priority rankings, waived first reading of several policies, and accepted the facilities report before entering executive session.

what_happened.line: The committee ratified a one-year para-professional contract by roll call, calling the raise modest given budget limits.
The committee approved FY26 capital-plan priority rankings, with the Primary School driveway ranked first and the playground second.
The committee accepted the facilities report and moved future reports to a written monthly submission instead of a live update.
The superintendent named the para-contract's cost, open teacher negotiations, health insurance and the bus contract bid as unresolved FY26 budget unknowns.
The committee reconsidered its adjournment to hear a resident's comment on DPW truck sequencing before entering executive session.

why_it_matters: The para-professional contract and unresolved teacher negotiations both feed directly into the FY26 school budget the town will eventually vote on.
The capital-plan rankings determine which building projects, including the Primary School driveway and playground, get funded first as FY26 capital dollars are allocated.
Moving facilities reporting to a written monthly submission changes how residents can track ongoing work like the Turkey Hill security and fire-alarm projects.
watch_next: October 16 meeting, where updated 2024-2025 school committee goals are due once MCAS data has been analyzed
Further FY26 budget timeline discussion as staff retention, salary competitiveness, health insurance and the bus contract bid are resolved

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every vote's outcome, the FY26 capital-plan figures, the para-professional 4% raise, and the chapter 90 figures, with most surface differences being predictable caption mishearings of names (Lehtinen→"Leon," Sculimbrene→"Scholbrini," Archambault→"Arshambo," Brzozoski→"Brzowski") and one garbled amount. The one figure a reader should check by hand is the town-manager recruiting-firm transfer: our captions have $115,000, the official minutes say $15,000 — an order-of-magnitude gap that should be confirmed against the Finance Committee/Select Board vote, not assumed to be a caption slip.
